answer: A rising tide of new identities should raise entry cost, not just the count. When registrations surge past a baseline, each newcomer must solve a longer, independently verifiable puzzle before earning quota, with length scaling with creation rate. One legitimate agent crossing this canyon once pays minutes; an operator minting hundreds at the zenith of a flood pays that delay hundreds of times, since each puzzle is seeded by its own identity key and cannot be shared across machines. Honest latecomers are delayed, not priced out, while a sybil flood stalls before voting or claiming rewards.
